title: Lobster Pasta With Tomatoes and Basil
description: This is an uncomplicated dish for warm weather and sunny days. Olive oil, garlic, hot pepper, barely warmed tomatoes and tons of fresh basil are the only ingredients besides lobster and dried pasta, preferably a variety with a bit of texture, like frilly edged reginette, cooked perfectly al dente. The only real work is cooking the lobsters and chopping the meat. Once that’s done, go out and enjoy the sunshine while it lasts.
ingredients: 4 lobsters, 1 1/4 pounds each, or 1 pound cooked lobster meat, or frozen lobster tails
1 pound sturdy pasta, like mafaldine, reginetti, lasagnetti, long ziti, macaroni, bucatini or rigatoncini – or really, whatever
2 cups chopped yellow tomato or halved yellow cherry tomatoes or a mix (the yellow doesn’t really add a lot)
2 handfuls basil leaves, torn or roughly chopped
directions: If using whole lobsters, cook them in abundant boiling water for 6 minutes. Or, cook the frozen lobster tails for 8 minutes.
Cool, remove meat from tail, claws and knuckles, and chop into 1/2-inch chunks.
Bring a pot of well-salted water to a boil and cook pasta.

Meanwhile, pour olive oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat. Add shallots and cook for 1 minute, without browning. Add garlic and red pepper and cook for 1 minute. Add tomatoes, season generously with salt and pepper, and cook for 1 minute. Add lobster meat, stir to coat, cook 1 minute, then turn off heat until pasta is ready.
When pasta is al dente, drain, add to skillet, and season with salt and pepper. Toss well and transfer to a warmed wide bowl or platter. Add basil, toss once more and serve immediately.
